error_unavailable: The server can't be reached right now. Please try again in a moment.
field_email_invalid: Please enter a valid email address.
login_error_credentials: Email address or password is wrong.
login_error_rate_limited: Too many attempts. Please try again in a minute.
login_expired: Your session has expired. Please sign in again.
login_setup_done: Setup is complete. Sign in with the new account now.
setup_subtitle: The first account becomes superadmin and creates the first organization.
setup_token_hint: Printed in the sermon-server log, valid for 30 minutes.
setup_error_token: The setup token is invalid or expired. A restart prints a new one to the log.
setup_error_invalid: The details don't meet the rules, e.g. the password is too simple or contains the name or email address.
command_palette_soon: The command palette follows in a later version.
fleet_empty_text: As soon as an agent is installed, the server shows up here with status and key figures. The install command is under “Add node”.
chart_empty: No data in the selected time range.
help_missing: There is no help for this topic yet.
stepup_text: Please enter your password again for this action. The confirmation lasts 15 minutes.
stepup_password_wrong: The password is wrong or the account is temporarily locked.
login_code_hint: Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app – or a recovery code.
login_error_code: The code is wrong or was already used – or the account is temporarily locked.
login_error_code_expired: Signing in took too long. Please sign in with your password again.
stepup_text_code: Please enter a code from your authenticator app (or a recovery code) for this action. The confirmation lasts 15 minutes.
security_2fa_text: In addition to the password, SerMon asks for a code from an authenticator app (e.g. Aegis, 2FAS, Google Authenticator).
security_2fa_required: This organization requires two-factor authentication. Please set it up now.
security_setup_scan: Scan the QR code with your authenticator app.
security_setup_qr: QR code for the authenticator app
security_setup_manual: Can't scan the QR code? Enter the key manually
security_setup_wrong_code: The code doesn't match. Check the device's clock and enter the current code.
security_setup_required_notice: This organization requires two-factor authentication. The other pages are available once it is set up.
security_codes_once: These codes are shown only now. Keep them safe: each code replaces the app once when it is not at hand.
security_disable_required: This organization requires two-factor authentication. Without it, its pages are no longer available.
fleet_table_caption: Nodes with status and key figures
node_not_found_text: The node doesn't exist, or it is in a group you may not see.
admin_error_forbidden: You lack the rights for this (admin of all groups).
admin_error_gone: That no longer exists – the view is refreshed.
admin_error_last_admin: The last admin of all groups can't be removed.
admin_invite_link: Invitation link – visible only now, because this server sends no mail (development). Pass it on securely; it works once within 72 hours.
admin_invite_sent: Invitation sent to {email}. The link works once within 72 hours; only this address receives it.
admin_2fa_text: When it is required, members without a second factor can only set one up. Your own account needs one first.
admin_2fa_own_first: Set up your own two-factor authentication first (page “Security”).
addnode_uses_hint: For several servers at once (e.g. with Ansible) raise the number of uses.
addnode_run_text: Paste it into a shell on the server (with sudo rights). The token travels in a variable, not in the process list. The script checks the agent's signature, creates the sermon user and connects the server.
addnode_self_signed: The server has no publicly trusted certificate (self-signed or own CA)
addnode_digest_failed: The checksum of the install script could not be loaded. Reload the page and try again.
addnode_fingerprint_invalid: Not a SHA-256 fingerprint (64 hex digits, colons optional).
addnode_fingerprint_hint: sha256:AB:CD:… – e.g. the output of openssl x509 -noout -fingerprint -sha256 -in cert.pem. The command checks install.sh against its checksum before sudo runs it.
addnode_fingerprint: Fingerprint of the server certificate or a CA
addnode_secret_once: The command contains a token and is visible only now.
addnode_forbidden: Operators and admins of a group may add nodes.
invite_invalid: The link is invalid, expired or already used.
invite_have_account: Already have an account? Sign in first, then open the link again.
invite_error_existing: There is already an account for this address – please sign in and open the link again.
invite_error_other_account: The invitation is for another email address.
addnode_no_groups: Nodes always belong to a group, and there is none yet. Admins create one under “Organization” → “Groups”.
alerts_empty_text: Everything is quiet. Alerts appear here as soon as a rule fires for one of your nodes. Which rules there are and where notifications go is explained in the help.
alert_muted_hint: A silence or maintenance window mutes the notifications of this alert.
alert_flapping_hint: The alert changes too often; its notifications are throttled.
alert_error_not_firing: The alert no longer fires or was acknowledged already. The list is up to date again.
alert_error_forbidden: You may not acknowledge this alert.
alert_source_unverified_note: Source not verified: a log file any local user can write to.
channel_secrets_note: Credentials are never shown. An empty field keeps the stored value.
channels_none: No channels yet. Create one so SerMon can report alerts.
deliveries_caption: Deliveries of the last 30 days, newest first
matchers_hint: Empty means all. Rule patterns with * (e.g. security.*), labels as key=value per line.
matchers_labels_invalid: Line {line} of the labels needs the form key=value.
notify_error_too_many_tests: Too many tests in a short time. Please wait a minute.
notify_error_too_many_channels: The organization already has the most channels allowed (50). Delete one before you add another.
policies_fallback: No policy yet: all alerts go to all enabled channels. As soon as there is a policy (even a disabled one), only the policies apply.
silence_nodes_hint: No selection means all nodes of the groups.
silences_intro: A silence mutes the notifications of matching alerts for a while (at most 30 days). The alerts stay visible; what still fires afterwards is sent once.
windows_intro: During a maintenance window “node offline” and “reboot” of the chosen groups are muted – every week at the same time.
rules_intro: The rules decide when an alert fires. SerMon ships default rules; admins can switch them off, adapt them as YAML or add their own. Rules are typed documents, not free queries.
rules_problem_stored: The stored version no longer loads, so the default rule applies: {message}
rules_checked: Checked, nothing stored. This would change:
identity_unlock_warning: The agent may connect again with its current key. If the key may have been stolen, revoke it instead and install the agent again.
identity_revoke_warning: All certificates of the node become invalid at once and its connection ends. Afterwards the agent has to be installed with a new token.
identity_rotated_online: The agent got a new key; the old one is revoked.
identity_rotated_offline: The node was not connected: its certificates are revoked and it has to be installed again.
identity_revoked: Revoked: the node has to be installed with a new token.
identity_takeover_done: Window open for an hour: install the agent again now with a token of this group.
lifecycle_scheduled: Deleted with all its data on {date}
lifecycle_deactivate_warning: The node's certificates are revoked and its connection ends at once. Metrics, events and logs stay, alerts rest. The node only comes back by “Allow takeover” and a new installation of the agent.
lifecycle_delete_warning: The node is deactivated at once and deleted with its metrics, events, alerts and logs after the grace (7 days by default). Until then the deletion can be cancelled.
lifecycle_delete_label: Type the host name {host} to confirm
lifecycle_deleted_done: The node will be deleted on {date}.
lifecycle_cancelled_done: Deletion cancelled; the node stays deactivated.
instance_dropped_security_events: {count} security events (logins, sudo, accounts) dropped within 15 minutes
instance_logs_unavailable: Logs can't be stored (Loki unavailable), log entries are dropped
tags_hint: key=value pairs separated by commas, e.g. env=prod, role=db. Keys: lowercase letters, digits, _ and -; values: letters, digits and _ . : / -.
tags_invalid: "{pair}" is not a valid tag (key=value, see the hint).
security_source_none_text: The agent finds neither journald nor a readable log file, so SSH logins, sudo and reboots of this node are not reported. On Alpine run
security_source_none_or: or set up the SerMon template for rsyslog.
security_source_unverified: Security events come from a log file and are not verified.
orgs_invite_sent: The invitation went to {email} by mail.
orgs_invite_link: No mail set up: pass this link to the first admin. It is shown only now.
orgs_quotas_hint: Empty means the instance default. At a quota new things are refused, what exists keeps running; a lowered quota deletes nothing.
orgs_quota_invalid: {field}: a whole number from 1 to {max}, or empty.
orgs_explain_lock: Members are signed out at once and can no longer enter the organization; agents are disconnected, enrollment tokens and invitations stop working. Alerts and notifications rest. Certificates and all data stay until you lift the lock. The admins get an email.
orgs_explain_schedule: Locks the organization like “Lock” and deletes it with all its data after the instance's grace period (default: 30 days). The admins get an email with the date and a reminder 7 days before. Until then you can lift the lock.
orgs_explain_unlock: Members sign in again, agents reconnect, alerts resume. A scheduled deletion is cancelled. The admins get an email.
orgs_explain_delete: Deletes the organization at once and for good: nodes, metrics, events, alerts, channels, the audit log and every account without another membership. Download the audit log first if you have to keep it.
orgs_done_schedule: “{name}” is locked and will be deleted on {date}.
orgs_done_delete: “{name}” is deleted; {accounts} accounts without another membership were removed.
orgs_export_done: Audit log downloaded; the hash chain is intact.
orgs_export_broken: Audit log downloaded – warning: the hash chain is broken, entries were changed afterwards.
orgs_error_not_locked: This works only for a locked organization.
admin_quotas_intro: The superadmin of the instance sets the quotas. At a quota new nodes and invitations are refused, what exists keeps running.
admin_error_quota: The organization's quota is reached; the superadmin can raise it.
logs_error_unavailable: The log store (Loki) is not reachable right now. Please try again shortly.
logs_error_forbidden: You may not see logs in this organization.
logs_error_invalid: The server does not accept this filter. Please check the time range and the input.
logs_error_too_many_live: Too many log queries or live views are running. Please wait a moment or close some and try again.
logs_filter_units_hint: systemd units or syslog identifiers, separated by commas.
logs_filter_text_hint: Part of the line, exactly as typed (no regular expression).
logs_histogram_failed: The histogram could not be loaded.
logs_histogram_summary: {count} lines from {from} to {to}. To zoom, drag across a part with the mouse or choose a range.
logs_lines_limit: At most {count} lines are shown. For older ones please narrow the range.
logs_context_text: Up to 50 lines before and after from {host}, unit {unit}. The entry is marked.
logs_empty_hint: Choose a longer range or remove filters. “Live” shows new lines.
logs_empty_no_nodes: No nodes yet. As soon as an agent runs, its logs show up here.
logs_live_on: Live: new lines appear at the top.
logs_live_throttled: More than 100 lines per second arrive; older ones were skipped. Narrow the filter or use the query.
logs_notice_vetoed: These nodes send no logs because their agent.toml forbids it (allow_logs = false): {hosts}.
logs_notice_lost: In this range the agent lost journal entries (approximate number): {hosts}. Lines are missing here.
chart_logs_link: Logs of this node in this range
logsettings_intro: What the agents send as logs, who sees them and what is redacted before. Every change asks for the password again.
logsettings_viewers_text: Logs and security events contain personal data. Without access only operators and admins see them.
logsettings_viewers_on: Viewers see logs and security events.
logsettings_viewers_off: Viewers see no logs and security events.
logsettings_groups_text: What the agents of a group's nodes send. Without settings of its own: logs on, everything.
logsettings_exclude_units_hint: systemd units or syslog identifiers, one per line or separated by commas.
logsettings_unit_invalid: Only letters, digits and @ : . _ \ - are allowed, at most 256 characters.
logsettings_files_hint: Absolute patterns with * and ?, e.g. /var/log/nginx/*.log. An entry starts with a line the regular expression matches; without one, indented lines belong to the entry before. The agents read only below the directories their host allows (default /var/log).
logsettings_file_multiline: Start of an entry in pattern {n}
logsettings_glob_segments: No empty segments, . or .. in the path.
logsettings_glob_wildcards: Only * and ? are wildcards; [ ] and \ are not supported.
logsettings_glob_duplicate: This pattern is in the list already.
logsettings_multiline_long: The expression for the start has at most 1,024 bytes.
logsettings_saved: Saved. Connected agents get it at once.
logsettings_rules_text: The agents always redact passwords, tokens and private keys. Your rules come on top: a regular expression replaces its match with ***, or only the group (?P<secret>…).
logsettings_test_result: This is how the agents would send the line with the rules in the form:
procs_status_paused_waiting: Paused – showing the state of {time}, newer data is waiting.
procs_status_offline: The agent is not connected to this server instance right now. The view continues as soon as it connects.
procs_refused: The agent refuses the live view: {reason}
procs_refused_hint: The host's agent.toml says allow_live_view = false. Only once that is changed and the agent restarted does it show its processes.
procs_failed_forbidden: You lack the right to see the processes of this node live.
procs_failed_not_found: The node doesn't exist, or you don't see it.
procs_failed_too_many: Too many live views are open at once. Close other tabs with live data and try again.
procs_waiting: Waiting for the agent's first data …
procs_omitted: The agent left out {count} more processes (at most 4,000, the busiest first).
procs_regex_invalid: Invalid regular expression, it doesn't filter: {detail}
procs_regex_too_long: The regular expression is too long (at most {max} characters), it doesn't filter.
procs_drawer_text: Read only: SerMon doesn't end or start processes.
procs_drawer_ended: The process is no longer running; showing its last state.
procs_cmdline_none: Kernel threads and zombies have no command line.
procs_cmdline_redacted: Secrets are replaced as in the logs.
logsettings_cmdline_title: Command lines in the live view
logsettings_cmdline_text: Command lines can contain secrets. When hidden, the agents no longer send them and the server removes them as well. Open live views reconnect within 30 seconds.
logsettings_cmdline_shown: Command lines are shown, with secrets replaced.
secdash_filter_network_invalid: Neither an address nor a network in CIDR notation.
secdash_error_forbidden: You lack the right to see security events, or the organization keeps them from viewers.
secdash_error_invalid: The filter is invalid. Check the IP or network and the time range.
secdash_no_nodes: No nodes yet – security events arrive once an agent is enrolled.
secdash_chart_empty: No failed logins in the range.
secdash_chart_failed: The overview is not available right now.
secdash_chart_summary: {count} failed logins on {nodes} nodes from {from} to {to}.
secdash_top_empty: No failed logins in the range.
secdash_empty_hint: Choose a longer time range or loosen the filter.
secdash_export_truncated: Saved the first {count} events as CSV – the export is bounded. Narrow the filter to get the rest.
alertstats_truncated: The range holds more history than one evaluation reads; the figures cover its older part.
alertstats_forbidden: You lack the right to see alerts.
sso_error_unavailable: The identity provider can't be reached right now. Try again later.
sso_failed: Signing in with the identity provider didn't work. Try again or sign in with your password. If you have no account yet, ask an admin of your organization.
sso_second_factor: Signed in at the identity provider. Now enter the code of your second factor.
stepup_text_sso: Confirm once more at the identity provider for this action.
stepup_sso_hint: You return to this page afterwards; run the action again then.
sso_text: Link your account with {name} to sign in there. You are recognized by your identity at the provider, not by your e-mail.
sso_taken: This identity is linked to another account already (or yours has one of this provider).
sso_unlink_last: This is your only way to sign in. Unlinking works once you have a password.
oidcmap_no_provider: The instance has no OIDC provider. Mappings take effect once the operator sets one up.
oidcmap_provisioning_on: At every sign-in the roles from mappings follow the groups. Unknown people of a mapped group get an account and become members.
oidcmap_provisioning_off: At every sign-in the roles from mappings follow the groups. The instance creates no accounts: people have to be invited.
oidcmap_group_hint: Exactly as in the "groups" claim, case-sensitive. Roles given by hand stay untouched.
admin_from_sso_hint: From an SSO group: the next sign-in may change it. Given by hand, it stays.
passkey_instead_of_code: Use a passkey instead of the code
stepup_text_passkey: Confirm once more with your passkey for this action.
passkey_text: With a passkey you sign in without a password – with the fingerprint, face recognition or PIN of your device or a security key. A passkey is also your second factor.
passkey_too_many: You have 10 passkeys already. Delete one first.
passkey_name_invalid: The name needs 1 to 64 characters without control characters.
orgs_error_lock_too_recent: The organization was locked just now. Deleting at once works 10 minutes after the lock: hosts with a clock ahead still send log lines that would be left over.
logs_error_too_broad: The query is too broad: too many nodes or too long lines. Please shorten the time range or choose a group or node.
updates_veto_updates: The host allows no remote updates (allow_remote_updates in /etc/sermon/helper.toml).
updates_veto_reboot: The host allows no remote reboot (allow_remote_reboot in /etc/sermon/helper.toml).
updates_refresh_requested: The agent lists the updates again; the report follows within minutes.
updates_refresh_too_soon: Listed a moment ago – try again in a few minutes.
updates_packages_omitted: The report lists not all {total} updates; all of the chosen scope are installed.
updates_started: Started – the rollout runs with the group's maxParallel.
updates_reboot_started: Reboot requested – the host reboots a minute after taking it.
runs_output_cut: The beginning of the output was cut.
runs_output_forbidden: The output is like a log of the host; you lack the right to read it.
policy_auto_reboot: Reboot after updates if needed (within the window)
policy_need_window: Automatic modes need a window with at least one day.
policy_alpine: Alpine nodes only report with "security updates automatically": Alpine has no security updates.
agent_install_package: as a package – the package manager updates it
agent_update_started: Started – the agent fetches the new version and restarts.
agent_veto: The host allows no remote agent updates (allow_self_update in /etc/sermon/helper.toml).
agent_helper_outdated: The root helper is older than the agent. Newer helpers update themselves with the agent – this one needs install.sh once more.
policy_agent_auto: Update the agent in the window (installations by install.sh)
unusual_hint: Mark a range in a chart (drag) and check it: SerMon lists the metrics with the highest scores.
unusual_too_old: Anomalies exist for the last 30 days.
anomalies_none: No anomaly rates yet: new nodes learn for 7 days before SerMon scores them.
capacity_no_filesystems: No file systems yet: the agents report them every 10 seconds.
capacity_truncated: Shown are the {count} that run full first or are the fullest.
capacity_trends_truncated: Trends are read for the first {count} nodes by host name; the fleet has more.
capacity_trends_hint: Mean of the last 7 days and the change against the first 7 of the 30 days (in percentage points).
heatmap_legend_text: Dark means little, bright much; empty cells have no data.
heatmap_truncated: Shown are the first {count} nodes by name.
heatmap_cursor_hint: Point at a cell, or focus the heatmap and move with the arrow keys.
heatmap_grid_label: {label} of {rows} nodes over time; arrow keys choose a cell
compare_intro: Two to four nodes over the same time range, side by side on one scale or overlaid.
compare_pick_hint: Choose at least {min} nodes to compare.
compare_limit: At most {max} nodes can be compared.
compare_no_data: No data in the time range: {hosts}
compare_no_nodes: No nodes yet – once an agent is installed, it can be compared here.
runs_cancel_too_late: The node has already started this run; it can't be cancelled any more.
rollout_cancel_text: Nodes still waiting are skipped; nodes updating right now finish without a reboot.
updates_paused_text: No rollout starts a node and no waiting run goes out; updates and reboots by hand are refused. Runs under way go to their end.
updates_pause_title: Pause all updates of the organization?
updates_pause_text: Until an admin resumes them, no rollout starts another node, waiting runs stay back and updates and reboots by hand are refused. Runs under way go to their end.
updates_paused_refused: The organization's updates are paused; an admin can resume them on the Updates page.
dashboards_intro: Your own dashboards and the ones shared in the organization. Every widget shows only data of the nodes you may see.
dashboards_import_too_large: The file is larger than 32 KiB.
dashboards_empty_hint: Give a new dashboard a title above, or import the JSON file of an exported one.
dashboard_missing: This dashboard does not exist or is not shared with you.
dashboard_conflict: Someone changed the dashboard meanwhile. Load it again and redo your change.
dashboard_empty: This dashboard has no widgets yet.
dashboard_empty_editing: Choose a kind and add the first widget.
dashboard_choices_failed: Metrics and nodes could not be loaded; try again later.
dashboard_full: A dashboard has at most {max} widgets, or the grid has no room left.
dashboard_forbidden: You may not change this dashboard.
dashboard_grid_hint: Arrow keys move the widget, Shift and arrow keys change its size, Delete removes it. Widgets in the way move down.
dashboard_grid_blocked: {title} cannot go there: the grid ends.
dashboard_form_text: What the widget shows and of which nodes.
dashboard_form_error_target: Choose the nodes: nodes, a group or a variable.
dashboard_form_error_single: A gauge or stat shows exactly one node: choose one node or a node variable.
dashboard_form_error_text: The text has at most {max} bytes on one line.
